# Phase Three — Tiferes Critique: Thirty-Two Final Refinements

The Awtsmoos joins expansion and restraint until a balanced vessel sings,
Awtsmoos.com should gain invisible depth while the user's path grows light with fewer things.
This third pass challenges even the careful second plan before a single source file turns,
Because durable simplicity is what remains when every unnecessary flourish burns.

## Thirty-two additional refinements

1. Apply HTML essentials only to complete documents with both closing head/body evidence; fragments must remain fragments.
2. Honor `data-g-ui-raw` in every new document transform, not only in CSS injection.
3. Viewport detection must be case-insensitive and tolerate attribute order.
4. Viewport injection must happen before `</head>` and be idempotent across repeated transforms.
5. Do not rewrite an authored viewport's content even if it differs from the default.
6. Skip navigation must never appear when no semantic `<main>` exists.
7. Existing main ids must be reused exactly rather than normalized or replaced.
8. Generated main ids must avoid duplication if the fallback id already exists elsewhere in the document.
9. Existing skip-navigation detection should recognize semantic intent through class/id or href-to-main patterns without claiming every fragment link is a skip link.
10. Generated skip-link text should be plain, short, and localization-neutral enough for the site's current English utility surfaces.
11. The generated skip link must be first meaningful body content so keyboard users encounter it immediately.
12. The skip link's hidden state must use transform/positioning rather than `display:none`, `visibility:hidden`, or zero-size tricks that remove it from accessibility flows.
13. Focus styling must use `:focus-visible`, not permanent focus chrome that increases visual noise for pointer users.
14. Focus fallback must not remove any authored outline; the universal layer should only add a readable default.
15. Forced-colors rules must use system colors instead of relying on custom palette variables.
16. High-contrast media rules should strengthen borders/focus, not globally recolor branded surfaces.
17. Fragment scroll spacing should target explicit ids without forcing page-wide scroll behavior.
18. Do not add JavaScript for any enhancement that HTML and CSS can deliver; less runtime machinery is better UX.
19. Do not add a global menu/compass in this pass; representative full-screen apps prove that fixed chrome would create layout and obstruction risk.
20. Keep the universal stylesheet source readable and modular while relying on the proven server-side CSS dependency folding for transport efficiency.
21. Structured-data evidence detection must be conservative: false positives are safer than silently duplicating authored schema on known public pages.
22. Generated marker detection remains first-class so idempotence stays cheap and exact.
23. JSON-LD detection must accept whitespace and quote variations around `type="application/ld+json"`.
24. Microdata detection should recognize schema.org itemtypes and plain `itemscope` evidence without trying to parse the full DOM with regex.
25. RDFa detection should recognize schema.org vocabulary/prefix evidence; unrelated RDFa must not necessarily suppress generated schema.
26. Strengthening the WebSite graph must keep the page/application/game canonical subject unchanged.
27. Use a stable `https://awtsmoos.com/#website` identity so all generated public pages refer to the same site entity.
28. Keep `WebSite` claims minimal: name and URL only, because no unverified logo, publisher, search action, or social profiles should be invented.
29. Do not add BreadcrumbList in this pass unless a verified semantic parent graph exists for every included route family; Apps/Games alone do not justify a partial hierarchy engine yet.
30. Test transformations as pure functions before runtime integration so regressions are attributable.
31. Runtime verification must include at least one page with authored viewport/skip behavior and one legacy page missing them, proving both preservation and supplementation.
32. Final completion requires git diff inspection against pre-existing dirty work so only intended central modules and new planning/test files are attributed to this pass.

## Final architecture decision

Use the existing shared response pipeline as the single amplification point. Add only pure, idempotent, opt-out-aware transforms and one low-specificity CSS module. Preserve all page-specific design systems and all existing SEO generator/sitemap architecture.

## Why the plan changed from phase one

The first phase considered centralized navigation, breadcrumb generation, broad route taxonomies, and richer schema families. Repository evidence showed that much of the crawl architecture already exists and that many public pages are specialist applications. The third plan therefore seeks greater effect through fewer interventions: response correctness, authored-truth preservation, universal mobile/accessibility essentials, and a stronger site graph.

## NEXT_ACTION

Write the final implementation contract with the exact files to create/rewrite, then implement complete files in one coding pass before tests.
